name: Darkish Red
lede: Darkish Red is a dark, brownish red recorded by the xkcd color survey, built from the modifier "darkish" on plain [[red]].

sections.title: Red, pushed dark
sections.body:
Our data traces Darkish Red to Wikipedia's color list and the 2010 xkcd crowd survey, with no earlier source on file [1]. Wikipedia gives a near-duplicate name, Rojo Spanish Red, only 2.1 units away in color [1]. The ISCC-NBS system does not carry this exact word; the nearest ISCC-NBS block name is "strong reddish brown", 6.1 units off [2]. Measured in Munsell notation the color is about 8.8R 3.5/13.7, a dark, fairly saturated red-brown [2].

The library's nearest named neighbor is [[deep-red]], which sits closer to a pure dark red, while Darkish Red leans brown [2]. Who first wrote "darkish red" down, and why, is undocumented in the sources we hold [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 99 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.4 percent, as photographed [3]. The earliest dated match is Niccolò di Pietro Gerini's 1391 *Madonna and Child, Four Saints and Four Angels*, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. The 1520s are its peak decade, at about six times the archive's overall rate [3]. Across all matches it plays a mid-tone four times out of five, rarely a shadow [3]. On the same canvases it keeps company most with [[brick]] and [[ochre]], at well above the rate chance would predict [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the matches are a computed color comparison, not a pigment identification [3].
